A story opens on a broken window, then cuts to breakfast. Why?

Many exam stories go wrong in one place. Beginning, middle or end?
A busy market, without the word 'busy'. Where do you point the camera?
component-2-19th-and-21st-century-non-fi: How do you crack a letter written 170 years ago?

Two writers, two centuries, one school day. Compare what, or how?
Two texts, a few lines. How do you sum them up without copying?
Same photo, charity advert and news report. Why such different words?
One writing task, the clock running. Why spend five minutes not writing?
Why does admitting the other side has a point make you stronger?
One opinion, a letter or a speech. What has to change?

An unexpected question. What do strong speakers do next?
